method: Independent lens review of captured evidence. The director opened every screenshot for a surface before scoring it, read the axe and capture results, and scored without sight of any other director's scores.
overallNote: Scored through the responsive, performance and production-quality lens only. The automated signal is genuinely clean across all ten app and six marketing captures: zero axe violations, zero console errors, HTTP 200 everywhere. The visual evidence is less settled. Three defects are measurable rather than matters of taste: the desktop Tasks List clips its Priority column at 1440px to unreadable stubs ('Hig', 'Lov', 'Nor') with no ellipsis or scroll affordance; the desktop Pricing fact band renders three supposedly identical cells at 533/374/533px with 160/27/27px of left padding, a defect the mobile version does not share and therefore proves is a bug; and Notes has two different centred max-widths stacked vertically (880 vs 947), producing a visible stair-step. A cross-cutting production issue: the fixed 'In development' toast overlays content on every app surface rather than reserving space, and on mobile it fully covers the Keep / Turn into task / Delete controls in Notes and a full row in Tasks List. Timeline is the standout — its horizontal axis is genuinely rebuilt as a vertical rail on mobile rather than squeezed — and the Tasks List's mobile card transformation is the second-best piece of responsive work. No surface warrants a veto; nothing here blocks a user or would disgrace the company, though the clipped Priority column and the broken pricing band would both be noticed immediately by a design-literate visitor. Significant evidence limits that I scored conservatively for rather than assuming the best: every capture is viewport-only (1440x900 and 390x844), so all below-fold layout is unassessed, including the Pricing plan cards, which are the single highest-risk responsive component on the marketing site. There is no capture at any intermediate breakpoint between 390 and 1440, which is exactly where the Tasks List table and the 1120px task modal are most likely to break. There is no CLS, LCP, bundle-size or font-loading data, no loading, skeleton, empty-under-load or error states, no zoom or 200% reflow evidence, and all demo content is short and well-behaved, so nothing here tests long titles, deep subtasks or real comment threads. None of the six scores should be read as evidence those conditions are handled.

surfaces.rationale: Confirmed by pixel crop: in the desktop List view at 1440px the Priority column is hard-clipped at the viewport edge — the header reads '⫼ P' and the values render as 'Hig', 'Lov', 'Nor', sliced mid-word with no ellipsis, no fade mask and no visible scroll affordance. A whole data column is unreadable at the most common laptop width, while the TASK column sits with ~250px of unused white space between the descriptions and the STATUS divider, so the space to fix it is already on screen. Table rows also run flush to x=1440 with no right gutter, unlike the Board view which respects a 12px margin. On the Board, the 'Menu tasting at The Orchard' card's meta row places 'Milestone due 1 Aug' flush against the card's right border with zero right padding, breaking the ~14px padding the rest of the card uses. Board card titles clamp on desktop ('Reprint the faded welcome sign before the open…', 'Send registrar paperwork two weeks before the…') while the identical titles render in full on mobile — truncation on the wider viewport, with several hundred px of empty column height below every stack. On mobile the board relies on two stacked horizontal scrollers (the To do/In progress/Review/Waiting chip row and the column strip), both clipped mid-item at x=390 with no gradient or peek treatment, so 'Menu ta…', 'Mara & F…' and 'Overdue…' are chopped mid-character. The mobile List transformation to stacked cards is the genuinely good piece of work here. Axe returned zero violations, console was clean and HTTP was 200 on all four captures.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Give the desktop List table a constrained TASK column and a proper horizontal scroll container with an edge fade, so Priority renders complete at 1440px instead of clipping to 'Hig'/'Lov'/'Nor' at the viewport edge.

surfaces.rationale: The desktop modal is the most structurally disciplined surface in the app set: 1120px wide, a clean two-column split at x=938, nothing overflows, and the fixed panel height means the layout will not jump as fields populate. The cost is visible emptiness — the metadata rail ends at y=657 leaving ~150px of void, the left column has a dead band under the 'Press e to open a task full-screen' hint, and the column divider stops at y=740 rather than meeting the panel floor, leaving a ragged 65px tail. On mobile the sheet adapts properly: the title wraps to two full lines, the To do / Orla / No due date / High chip row fits 390px without wrapping awkwardly, and 'Mark done' drops to its own row rather than compressing. A zoomed crop of the mobile top edge shows a low-contrast grey rounded shape bleeding off the top of the sheet around x=20–187, y=0–10 — a leftover chrome or grabber artifact at the very first thing the eye lands on. The mobile stacking order also pushes REPEATS, TAGS, CONTACT, PROJECT and SOURCE below the conversation composer, so the fold cuts at TAGS and the key metadata sits behind a long scroll past an empty comment thread. What the evidence cannot show, and where I give no credit: this is one short task with a one-line description, no subtasks, no attachments and an empty conversation. The two-column modal is untested against long descriptions, deep subtask trees or a real comment thread, and there is no intermediate-width capture where a 1120px modal must collapse.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Move the metadata rail (contact, project, source, dates) above the conversation in the mobile stack so the fields are reachable without scrolling past an empty comment thread, and clear the grey artifact bleeding off the sheet's top edge.

surfaces.rationale: Desktop has a measurable container mismatch: the composer card spans x=310–1190 (880px) while the search row and the list/reader panes below span x=275–1222 (947px), both centred on the same axis. The result is a 35px stair-step on each side — the composer's left edge does not line up with the note list's left edge, and the rule under the search row stops 32px short of the reader pane's content edge. The reader is also very sparse: a three-line note leaves roughly 330px of void between the body and the Captured/Edited footer pinned at the bottom. On mobile the surface loses content rather than adapting it — the tab counts (Notebook 14, Review 8, In Tasks 6) are dropped entirely, and the 'Newest first' sort control disappears leaving only 'All notes'. The '/' keyboard shortcut hint is still rendered in the search field on a touch device where no keyboard exists. A zoomed crop shows the active 'Notebook' pill starting at x=8 against a 16px page gutter used by the composer card below it, with asymmetric internal padding — the label sits hard against the pill's left edge with ~36px of slack on the right. Worst of all on mobile, the fixed 'In development' toast lands directly on top of the Keep / Turn into task / Delete row, fully obscuring three interactive controls; the toast overlays rather than reserving space, so it will always cover whatever is at that scroll position. Axe clean, console clean, HTTP 200.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Unify the composer and the list/reader panes to a single max-width so their vertical edges align, and stop the fixed toast from overlaying interactive rows — reserve space for it or offset the scroll container's bottom padding.

surfaces.rationale: This is the strongest responsive thinking in the set. The desktop horizontal axis with alternating above/below milestone labels is not squeezed or side-scrolled on mobile — it is rebuilt as a genuine vertical rail with dot, label and date stacked, which is a real rethink rather than a reflow. Nothing clips or overflows at either width, the 'Mara & Finn' display type holds on one line at 390px, and the countdown block (79 days / 2 of 9 complete / Wedding day · 3 Oct 2026) reflows cleanly from the desktop right rail into the mobile stack. Two precision defects on desktop: the right quarter of the axis is congested — five unlabelled hollow dots between x=1151 and x=1329 collapsed under a single '4 milestones' bracket, so a third of the timeline carries no readable information while the left two-thirds is sparsely populated; and the 'Today' label sits at y=664 against the month labels' y=660, a 4px baseline break on the one element where alignment precision is most legible. On mobile the Timeline/Milestones/Preview/Share control row ends at x=357 against a 16px left gutter, an asymmetric right margin. The toast again covers the second timeline entry. Evidence limits I will not give credit for: only about 1.5 milestones are visible above the mobile fold, the Preview and Share states are uncaptured despite 'sharing' being in this surface's scope, and no capture shows the axis under a denser milestone set where the right-hand cluster would get worse.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Resolve the crowded right-hand milestone cluster on the desktop axis — either distribute the five unlabelled dots with real labels or make the '4 milestones' group an explicit expandable marker, so the last quarter of the timeline carries readable information.

surfaces.rationale: The cleanest surface from my lens. No overflow, no clipping, no truncation at either width. The hero headline scales properly from four lines at 1440 to four shorter lines at 390 with no awkward orphan or horizontal bleed, the two CTAs sit side by side on desktop and go full-width stacked on mobile, and the 'NOTES → TASKS → TIMELINE' eyebrow survives both. HTTP 200, zero console errors, zero axe violations at both viewports. The grid relationship is the unresolved part: the nav logo sits at x=122 and 'About' ends at x=1294, but the entire hero column starts at x=280 and runs to ~1160, an axis nothing else above the fold picks up — it reads as an unresolved inset rather than a deliberate editorial offset. Below the hero there is a large dead band from y=694 to the section rule at y=832 with nothing in it. On mobile the header carries both a visible 'Products' dropdown and a hamburger, a redundant pair of navigation affordances competing in a 390px bar. What the evidence cannot show, and I score conservatively for: this is the page where performance matters most and I have no LCP, no CLS, no bundle size, no font-loading behaviour, and no full-page capture — the hero is pure type with no imagery to stress, so the sections below the fold, which are where marketing pages actually accumulate layout shift, are entirely unassessed.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Align the hero column to the same container as the header (x=122) or commit the header to the hero's 280 axis, so the page resolves onto one grid instead of two competing ones.

surfaces.rationale: The editorial device — purple dot, 'A NOTE FROM THE FOUNDER' eyebrow, and a vertical rule descending the full page at x=96 — survives both viewports intact, and the four-line headline scales from ~64px to ~28px without a single bad break or overflow. Desktop shows a container mismatch: the body paragraph's longest line runs to x=1319 while the nav's right boundary sits at x=1294, so the prose measure is wider than the header container it should be nested in. The desktop fold is also very thin — the single visible paragraph is pushed into the right half starting at x=732 and y=688, leaving an empty L roughly 600×300px in the bottom-left quadrant; at 1440×900 a visitor sees a headline and one paragraph of body copy with a large void between them. Mobile is the better composition: the rail, headline, body and the bold 'The mistake was assuming every project should work that way' pull-line all stack cleanly at a 24px gutter. A 4x crop of the mobile rail at y=755–844 shows two hollow node markers 17px apart at different x offsets (one at x≈33 fed by a horizontal tick, one at x≈12 sitting on the rail with a stub), overlapping each other and colliding with the left edge of the 'A wedding may be the largest project someone ever manages' heading. That reads as a duplicated or mispositioned marker rather than an intentional pair. Axe clean, console clean, HTTP 200. Only the first screen of a long-form essay page is captured, so the rest of the article's rhythm is unassessed.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Fix the doubled, colliding node markers on the mobile rail at the 'A wedding may be the largest project…' section break — one marker, aligned to the rail, clear of the heading's left edge.

surfaces.rationale: I measured the desktop fact band by pixel-scanning the divider positions: the band spans full-bleed x=0–1440 at y=500–577 with dividers at exactly x=533 and x=907, giving three cells of 533 / 374 / 533px. Their content starts at x=160, 560 and 934 — left padding of 160px, 27px and 27px. So three visually identical cells are unequal in width, the first item's label floats 160px from its own cell edge to meet the page grid while the other two sit hard against their dividers, and the third cell trails ~400px of empty space to the viewport edge. The mobile capture confirms this is a bug and not a stylistic choice: the same three facts stack with consistent 24px padding and even dividers, and read correctly. The desktop hero also leaves the entire right half (x≈830–1440) empty above the band. Mobile is otherwise sound — hero type scales, no overflow, the band bleeds edge to edge with content on the 24px gutter. Axe clean, console clean, HTTP 200 at both widths. The decisive evidence limit: on a pricing page the plan cards are the content most likely to truncate, overflow or collapse badly, and they sit below the fold on both viewports in these viewport-only captures. Four tiers ('Four ways in') are promised and none are visible. I will not give credit for layout I cannot see, and this score reflects a surface whose highest-risk component is unassessed.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Rebuild the three-up fact band as an even grid inside the page container — equal cell widths with matched padding — instead of a full-bleed band whose first cell carries 160px of left padding and the others 27px.
